nodes.name: Thermal Nanoimprint Lithography
nodes.procedure: Deep cylindrical holes (diameter: 3.5 μm, depth: 16 μm) were formed in polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) substrates using thermal nanoimprint lithography (T-NIL).
nodes.source_text: First, the deep cylindrical holes (diameter: 3.5 μm, depth: 16 μm) were formed in a polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) substrates using thermal nanoimprint lithography (T-NIL)

nodes.name: Nickel Seed Layer Deposition
nodes.procedure: The inner surfaces of the holes except the bottom surfaces of the PMMA hole was then coated with a 30-nm-thick nickel (Ni) seed layer by glancing angle deposition (GLAD).

nodes.name: Microcurrent Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Subsequent microcurrent electrodeposition of Ni enabled the uniform growth of sidewalls on the top of the seed layer, where the thickness of electrodeposited Ni could be precisely controlled by changing the microcurrent and electroplating time.

nodes.name: Template Removal and Acid Etching
nodes.procedure: The PMMA templates were removed with CH₂Cl₂ to reveal the nickel tube arrays (NTA), which was then treated with acid to obtain the porous nickel tube arrays (PNTA).

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Growth + Selective Etching
nodes.procedure: The NiFeZn-nanosheets were grown on PNTA by hydrothermal method, following selective alkaline etching of the Zn²⁺ to create Zn²⁺ pores (P_Zn) in the nanosheets. The NiFe-P_Zn grow on both inner and outer surfaces of the PNTA after hydrothermal reaction. The isolated NiFe-P_Zn with a thickness around 8 nm are vertically anchored on the tube wall.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping confirms uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, and O on NiFe-P_Zn@PNTA with no Zn observed, indicating successful Zn^{2+} etching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping results confirm a uniform distribution of nickel, iron, and oxygen on the NiFe- P_{Zn}@PNTA. Notably, zinc (Zn) was not observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: PNTA shows Ni (111), (200), (220) peaks at 44.3°, 51.8°, 76.3°; NiFe-P_Zn@PNTA shows additional NiFe-P_Zn (003), (006), (012), (015), (110), (133) peaks confirming successful loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The PNTA has three distinct diffraction peaks at 44.3°, 51.8° and 76.3° correspond to the (111), (200), and (220) planes of Ni. In addition to the above three characteristic peaks, the other peaks centered at 11°, 22.5°, 33.1°, 35.6°, 62.5° and 64° for the NiFe- P_{Zn}@PNTA correspond to the (003), (006), (012), (015), (110) and (133) facets of the NiFe- P_{Zn}.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe 2p shows Fe^{3+} at 711.4 eV (2p_{3/2}) and 723.5 eV (2p_{1/2}); Ni 2p shows Ni^{2+} at 854.5 eV (2p_{3/2}), 872.2 eV (2p_{1/2}) with 0.4 eV redshift vs PNTA due to Fe incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe 2p spectrum could be deconvoluted into Fe 2p_{3/2} peak at 711.4 eV and Fe 2p_{1/2} peak at 723.5 eV... the Ni 2p spectrum is consisting of Ni 2p_{1/2} and Ni 2p_{3/2} peaks located at 872.2 eV and 854.5 eV, respectively, corresponding to Ni^{2+} cations.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (C_dl) measured via CV in double layer region estimates ECSA of 66.00 cm² for NiFe-P_Zn@PNTA, 47.75 cm² for NiFe@PNTA, 7.25 cm² for PNTA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The double-layer capacitance (C_dl, Figure S18, Supporting Information) was measured via cyclic voltammetry in the double layer regions with different scan rates (Figure. S19, Supporting Information) to estimate the electrochemical active surface area (ECSA). The ECSA of the NiFe- P_{Zn}@PNTA electrode is 66.00 cm².

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows R_ct of 0.2 Ω for NiFe-P_Zn@PNTA, 0.3 Ω for NiFe@PNTA, 0.5 Ω for PNTA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The R_ct of NiFe- P_{Zn}@PNTA is determined to be about 0.2Ω, which is smaller than that of NiFe@PNTA (0.3Ω) and PNTA (0.5Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman shows transformation from Ni(OH)_2 to NiOOH at 1.40 V (472 cm^{-1} peak), and Ni(Fe)OOH formation at 1.54 V (553 cm^{-1} Ni-O, 691 cm^{-1} Fe-O peaks).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S24 (Supporting Information), the transformation from Ni(OH)_2 into NiOOH starts at 1.40 V based on the appearance of a new Raman peak located at 472 cm^{-1}. When the potential reaches to 1.54 V, two additional Raman peaks located at 553 cm^{-1} and 691 cm^{-1} are generated, belonging to the Ni-O and Fe-O vibrations in amorphous Ni(Fe)OOH.
